subject: Discovery confirmation + POC manifest / next steps for Lumenix
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@lumenix.com>, Priya Singh <priya@lumenix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Discovery confirmation + initial POC manifest

Carlos / Priya — thanks again for carving out time this morning. Quick written recap so we have shared clarity and immediate next steps for the 30-day POC we discussed.

Highlights (pain & goal)
- Pain: Lumenix is seeing production inference latency spikes (p95 ~900ms) and token costs that make scaled retrieval/real-time features prohibitively expensive. You also noted occasional generation drift on critical fields.
- Goal: Validate a serving configuration that reduces p95 latency to <350ms (target p50 <150ms) for the main conversational path, while reducing per-1k-token cost by at least 30% relative to your current endpoint. Secondary goal: ensure data controls for EU residency for certain customers.

Proposed 30-day POC scope (manifest)
- Duration: 30 days starting once access is provisioned.
- Workloads: two primary flows — real-time chat (short context, ~512 tokens) and batch summarization (longer context, ~4–8k tokens).
- Success metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens per second, cost per 1k tokens, and quality delta on your prompt set (ROUGE-like score + manual checks on 20 critical prompts).
- Owners: Technical lead (Lumenix): Carlos Vega. Redwood: Neha Kapoor (solutions), Marissa Cole (AE), Karthik Iyer (deal owner).

Immediate asks / access checklist (what we need by EOD Friday)
1) Sample prompt set & evaluation rubric (20 prioritized prompts + acceptance criteria).
2) Short-term access: temp API key or test endpoint + one sample dataset (S3 presigned or share link).
3) Network: confirm whether you prefer hosted (Redwood API) or private VPC peering for the pilot; if VPC, we’ll need CIDR and oncall contact.
4) Compliance note: if EU-residency is needed, flag which customer segments to scope.

Attachments: I’ve attached an initial POC manifest and a blank mutual action plan for you to review.

Next proposals
- Kickoff session (technical) — propose Tue 2026-08-10 10:00am PT. 45m to align owners, access, and baseline metrics.
- Midpoint check (week 2) and acceptance review (day 30).

If that aligns, reply with: 1) confirmation of kickoff slot, 2) how you’ll share the prompt set, and 3) whether you want Redwood to start on hosted mode or require a private deployment for the POC.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

—
Karthik Iyer

Karthik — thanks for the tidy summary. Confirming a few items and adding context from our side.

On pain/priority
- Latency is top priority for our customer-facing chat product (latency spikes cause session drop and measurable conversion loss). Cost improvements will unlock rolling this feature out to our premium tier.
- Generation drift: examples attached in a separate doc (will share via Drive).

On scope & owners
- Confirming Carlos = technical owner, Priya = product sponsor. Please list Priya on all billing/contract conversations.

Access and timeline
- We can share a sanitized prompt set + rubric by 2026-08-06.
- For the POC we prefer Redwood hosted initially (faster onboarding). If the hosted results are promising we’ll evaluate Dedicated / Private for production.
- Kickoff slot on Tue 2026-08-10 10:00am PT works for Carlos & Priya.

Questions
1) Can Redwood provide a sample config that targets p95 <350ms for short-context chat (we’d like a sanity check before kickoff)?
2) For billing, do you require a signed MSA before starting a short proof, or can we run the pilot under a trial agreement?

Adding technical access steps and a pared-down checklist so your infra team can action quickly. Attachment: lumenix-poc-manifest.xlsx (worksheets: manifest, metrics, access).

Technical checklist (short)
1) Share a zipped sample dataset (anonymized) or provide S3 path + read-only IAM role / presigned URLs.
2) Provide test accounts and a minimal traffic profile (1–5 concurrent virtual users) so we can baseline latency.
3) If you choose hosted mode: provide a list of IPs we should allow for your systems to call back, and confirm whether you need EU-only storage for any artifacts.
4) If you later move to private mode: we’ll need VPC peering info (CIDR), a route table contact, and a maintenance window for the initial sync.

Config note
- I’ll preseed a config that uses 4-bit quantization + dynamic batching tuned for short-context chat; this typically reduces cost ~25–40% with small quality impact. We’ll include a control model to check quality regression on your 20-priority prompts.

Anticipated timeline
- Access + prompt set in by 2026-08-06 -> baseline profiling by 2026-08-07 -> deployed test endpoint by 2026-08-11 (post-kickoff).

Attachments: lumenix-poc-manifest.xlsx (spreadsheet), mutual-action-plan-lumenix.pdf (blank MAP).
